nodes.content: Design asynchronous distributed checkpointing that preserves recoverable training-state consistency across worker failures and changes in model parallelism.
requirements: Recover a committed, globally consistent model, optimizer, and RNG state after any single-worker crash.
Support restores across tensor-parallel layouts while limiting checkpoint-induced throughput loss to 5% versus checkpoint-free training.

nodes.content: Use step-aligned copy-on-write model, optimizer, and logical RNG snapshots; asynchronously upload globally indexed shards before atomic manifest commit.
Can step-boundary copy-on-write capture align optimizer and RNG versions across ranks without exceeding 5% throughput loss?
At 1,000-step intervals, a post-update rank barrier plus copy-on-write capture preserves identical state step IDs with ≤5% throughput loss.
Benchmark 8-rank training for 20,000 steps, checkpointing every 1,000 steps; compare state step IDs and tokens/second against checkpoint-free training.
Across 20 snapshots, all eight ranks matched model, optimizer, and RNG step IDs; throughput fell 3.4% versus checkpoint-free training.
Inject 250-ms rank jitter and 2-second upload stalls; verify snapshot step IDs and throughput loss against checkpoint-free training.
With 250-ms rank jitter and 2-second upload stalls, state step IDs matched, but throughput dropped 8.2% versus checkpoint-free training.
Capture post-sync state without checkpoint barriers; staged uploads maintain matching step IDs and ≤5% loss under jitter and stalls.
Repeat the 20,000-step jitter-and-stall benchmark, comparing barrier snapshots with barrier-free staged uploads on step-ID agreement and throughput loss.
Without upload stalls, barriers matched step IDs at 4.4% loss; under stalls, barrier-free uploads mixed step IDs in 4/20 snapshots.
How can barrier-free uploads reject mixed-step shards before manifest commit without stalling training?
A coordinator committing only complete, matching step-tagged shard sets prevents mixed snapshots without exceeding 5% throughput loss under upload stalls.
Replay n9's four mixed-step snapshots through coordinator validation, then benchmark 20,000 stalled steps for mixed commits and throughput.
Coordinator rejected all four replayed mixed snapshots; stalled benchmark committed 16/20 matched snapshots with 4.8% throughput loss.
Restore committed manifests, reshard globally indexed model and optimizer tensors across tensor-parallel degrees, and remap logical RNG streams.
How should globally indexed Adam moments and logical RNG streams map from TP=8 to TP=4 without changing resumed updates?
Global-offset resharding of weights and Adam moments plus sample-indexed Philox yields bitwise RNG matches and ≤1e-5 TP=8→4 update error.
Restore a committed TP=8 checkpoint at TP=4; compare next-step Adam updates against TP=8 and per-sample Philox draws bitwise.
Weights and Adam moments resharded exactly; shard-dependent Philox consumption changed 7% of dropout draws, yielding 2.3e-4 update error.
Repeat TP=8→4 restore with dropout disabled, then trace sample-indexed Philox counters and Adam update errors with dropout enabled.
Sample-and-global-offset Philox counter replay matched dropout draws bitwise and reduced TP=8→4 dropout-enabled update error to 6e-6.
Can fused-attention dropout preserve global-offset Philox replay when restoring TP=8 checkpoints at TP=2 with different attention tile sizes?
Element-indexed Philox counters for fused-attention dropout preserve bitwise masks across TP=8→2 tile changes and ≤1e-5 update error.
Reproduce n17’s TP=8→4 dropout mismatch as negative control; replay n19’s corrected counters through TP=8→2 fused-attention tiles, checking masks and updates.
Negative control reproduced 7% mismatched draws; TP=8→2 element-indexed replay matched fused-attention masks bitwise, with 8e-6 update error.
Replay n17’s mismatched and n19’s corrected counters across ragged 64/128-token attention tiles; compare TP=8→2 masks and update errors.
Ragged 64/128-token tiles caused 1.1% mask mismatches with corrected counters, yielding 4e-5 TP=8→2 update error.
Absolute sample/layer/head/query/key Philox counters, independent of tile padding, yield bitwise ragged masks and ≤1e-5 TP=8→2 update error.
Run TP=8→2 fused-attention restore on n23’s dense and n25’s ragged tiles using absolute-coordinate Philox; compare masks and update errors.
Absolute-coordinate counters matched dense and ragged attention masks bitwise; TP=8→2 next-step update error was 7e-6.
Persist checksum-verified shards in durable object storage; fence stale worker epochs and restore only complete, atomically committed manifests.
If a worker crashes during upload, can epoch fencing prevent its delayed shards from entering a replacement worker’s committed manifest?
Epoch-scoped shard keys plus compare-and-swap manifest commits reject late uploads after worker replacement and preserve the previous recoverable checkpoint.
Crash one uploader mid-checkpoint, replace its epoch, release delayed uploads, and verify manifest fencing and previous-checkpoint restore.
In 3/100 crash races, delayed epoch-7 shards completed stale manifests after epoch-8 replacement; unchanged-head CAS accepted them.
Pause epoch-7 manifest CAS, advance membership to epoch 8 without changing HEAD, then resume CAS and test restore.
Epoch-7 CAS succeeded against unchanged HEAD, but epoch-scoped keys isolated its shards; epoch-filtered restore recovered the previous checkpoint.
How can manifest commits atomically validate membership epochs when HEAD remains unchanged across worker replacement?
A linearizable transaction checking membership epoch and HEAD version rejects stale commits while retaining the latest valid checkpoint after crashes.
Replay n32’s crash races and n34’s unchanged-HEAD schedule with transactional epoch-plus-HEAD validation; verify stale-commit rejection and latest-valid-checkpoint restore.
Across 100 replayed crash races and unchanged-HEAD replacement, transactions rejected every stale commit and restored the latest valid checkpoint.
Epoch-scoped keys and transactional epoch-plus-HEAD validation reject stale manifests, preserving the latest complete checkpoint after worker replacement.
Run 500 worker-replacement races comparing HEAD-only CAS against transactional epoch-plus-HEAD validation; measure stale commits and recoverable checkpoint age.
HEAD-only CAS blocked 480/480 stale commits after HEAD advanced; epoch reuse let transactional validation accept 2/20 stale manifests.
How can worker incarnation IDs prevent epoch reuse from admitting stale manifests despite transactional membership checks?
Transactionally validating nonreusable worker-incarnation UUIDs and HEAD rejects stale manifests even when numeric epochs are reused.
Replay epoch-reuse, delayed-upload, and unchanged-HEAD races with transactional incarnation UUID validation; measure stale commits and latest-checkpoint restore.
Across 500 replayed races, incarnation UUID validation rejected every stale manifest; all restores selected the latest complete checkpoint.
Benchmark 20,000-step incarnation-fenced TP=8→2 restores with crashes, corrupt shards, ragged attention, and upload stalls; measure state consistency and throughput loss.
Across 100 single-worker crashes, TP=8→2 restores recovered consistent model/optimizer/RNG states; corrupt shards were rejected; throughput dropped 4.9% versus checkpoint-free training.
From n47’s recovered states, crash the coordinator before and after HEAD commit; compare visible manifest completeness and model/optimizer/RNG hashes.
After HEAD commit, 2/100 coordinator crashes exposed unpromoted optimizer shards; committed restores failed despite matching model/RNG hashes.
How can HEAD publication guarantee optimizer shards are durable and readable before coordinator crashes expose a committed checkpoint?
Durable-read verification of immutable final-key model, optimizer, and RNG shards before transactional HEAD publication prevents coordinator-crash restore failures.
Replay n49’s 100 coordinator crashes against n47’s states, durable-read all final-key shards before HEAD, then verify committed restores.
All 100 coordinator-crash replays restored complete model/optimizer/RNG states; no committed manifest referenced an unreadable shard.
Adopt durable-read checks of all final-key shards before incarnation-fenced HEAD commits; crash restores passed, but revalidate 4.9% overhead.
Implement durable-read gating; rerun 20,000-step worker/coordinator crash and TP=8→2 restores, validating model/optimizer/RNG consistency and ≤5% throughput loss.
Implement final-key durable-read gating; inject 100 worker/coordinator crashes during 20,000-step TP=8→2 training and measure restore consistency and throughput.
CrashRestore-20K report records 100 injected failures, TP=8→2 model/optimizer/RNG restore checks, shard-read validation, and checkpoint-free throughput comparison.
